package.name: gtm
package.packageFile:
# Two vendors, one package: Apollo.io for company and people data, Hunter.io for email.
# One credential each, one base URL each, no SDKs.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/gtm/`.

name: gtm
displayName: Go To Market
description: Company and people discovery, enrichment and email verification
version: 2.0.0
category: productivity
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775374180/gravity/icons/apollo.jpg

features:
  - Apollo company and people search, with filters
  - Apollo company and people enrichment
  - Hunter email discovery, finding and verification

allowedHosts:
  - api.apollo.io
  - api.hunter.io

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [page]
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.apolloCredential.yaml:
name: apolloCredential
displayName: Apollo.io
description: Apollo.io master API key for people and organisation search
documentationUrl: https://docs.apollo.io/docs/create-api-key

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Apollo.io master API key, required for the search endpoints
    placeholder: ""
credentials.hunterCredential.yaml:
name: hunterCredential
displayName: Hunter.io
description: Hunter.io API key for email discovery, verification and enrichment
documentationUrl: https://hunter.io/api-documentation/v2

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Hunter.io API key, found under API in your Hunter dashboard
    placeholder: ""

shared.apollo.yaml:
# What every Apollo call shares.
#
# The key travels in the `x-api-key` HEADER, which is `apiKeyHeader`, an executor
# capability. `Cache-Control: no-cache` is sent because the retired client sent it: Apollo
# is documented as caching search responses, and dropping the header would silently change
# which results come back.

credential: &credential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: x-api-key
  value: "{{ credentials.apolloCredential.apiKey }}"

headers: &headers
  Cache-Control: no-cache

# NOTE for the bodies below: every filter is a comma-separated config field turned into the
# array Apollo wants, with
#
#   String(config.x || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
#
# and an EMPTY array is left out of the body rather than sent, because Apollo reads an empty
# filter as "match nothing" rather than as "no filter". That is why each body is built by an
# expression that assembles only the keys that have values, instead of a static object.
shared.hunter.yaml:
# What every Hunter call shares.
#
# TWO auth styles, and that is Hunter's doing rather than ours: `/discover` takes the key in
# an X-API-KEY header, every other endpoint takes it as an `api_key` query parameter. Both
# are executor capabilities, so each call names the one its endpoint wants.

queryCredential: &queryCredential
  scheme: apiKeyQuery
  param: api_key
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

headerCredential: &headerCredential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: X-API-KEY
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

# Hunter wraps every payload in `data` and reports failures in `errors`, sometimes with a
# 200. Without this a quota error would emit an empty result and read as "not found".
error: &error
  when: "return !!(response.errors && response.errors.length)"
  message: "return response.errors.map(e => e.details || e.id).join('; ')"

# A LinkedIn URL to the handle Hunter wants. split/join rather than a regex, because the
# expression sandbox takes no regex literal: everything after /in/, up to a ? or #, with any
# trailing slash removed.
linkedinHandle: &linkedinHandle >-
  return String(config.linkedinHandle || '').trim()
    .split('/in/').slice(-1)[0]
    .split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
    .split('/').filter(Boolean).slice(-1)[0] || ''

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: email
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || {}).email || ''"

- emit: score
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || {}).score || 0"

- emit: position
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || {}).position || ''"

- emit: linkedin_url
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || {}).linkedin_url || ''"

- emit: verification_status
  from: response
  value: "return ((response.data || {}).verification || {}).status || ''"

- emit: sources_count
  from: response
  value: "return ((response.data || {}).sources || []).length"
files.api/run.yaml:
# One GET. Only the identifiers actually given are sent, because a blank parameter narrows
# the match rather than being ignored.
#
# `full_name` WINS over first and last: sending all three makes Hunter treat them as
# competing constraints. The retired code had the same either/or and it is easy to lose.

- name: find
  method: GET
  url: https://api.hunter.io/v2/email-finder
  credential: { $ref: hunter#queryCredential }
  query:
    linkedin_handle: { $ref: hunter#linkedinHandle }
    domain: "return String(config.domain || '').trim()"
    company: "return String(config.company || '').trim()"
    full_name: "return String(config.fullName || '').trim()"
    first_name: >-
      return String(config.fullName || '').trim() ? '' : String(config.firstName || '').trim()
    last_name: >-
      return String(config.fullName || '').trim() ? '' : String(config.lastName || '').trim()
  transport: json
  error: { $ref: hunter#error }
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    linkedinHandle:
      type: string
      title: LinkedIn Handle or URL
      description: A handle, or a full profile URL. The URL is reduced to the handle for you.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    domain:
      type: string
      title: Domain
      description: The person's company domain, e.g. 'google.com'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    company:
      type: string
      title: Company
      description: The company name, when you do not have the domain
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    fullName:
      type: string
      title: Full Name
      description: Takes precedence over first and last name when set
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    firstName:
      type: string
      title: First Name
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    lastName:
      type: string
      title: Last Name
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order": [linkedinHandle, domain, company, fullName, firstName, lastName]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger. The identifiers usually template from upstream output.

outputs:
  - name: email
    type: string
    description: The most likely address, or empty when none was found
  - name: score
    type: number
    description: Confidence 0-100
  - name: position
    type: string
    description: The person's job title, when known
  - name: linkedin_url
    type: string
    description: Their LinkedIn profile, when known
  - name: verification_status
    type: string
    description: Hunter's own verification status for the address, when available
  - name: sources_count
    type: number
    description: How many public sources back the address

credentials:
  - name: hunterCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Hunter.io
files.node.yaml:
type: HunterEmailFinder
kind: PromiseNode
name: Hunter Email Finder
category: Go To Market
color: "#FF5500"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1781366295/gravity/icons/hunter.png
description: Find one person's work email from their LinkedIn or their name and company
whenToUse: >
  Pick when you have a person's LinkedIn profile (handle or URL) or their name plus a
  company or domain, and need ONLY their work email and a confidence score. Use it to find
  one specific person's address; listing every address at a domain, verifying
  deliverability, or a full profile are different jobs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  cacheable: true

# One vendor. The package allows Apollo too, for its other four nodes.
allowedHosts: [api.hunter.io]
files.test.yaml:
testData:
  config:
    linkedinHandle: ""
    domain: close.io
    company: ""
    fullName: Steli Efti
    firstName: ""
    lastName: ""
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    # A miss is a valid outcome, so this asserts the contract rather than a hit.
    email: "return typeof output.email === 'string'"
    score: "return typeof output.score === 'number' && output.score >= 0"
